topics.title: Unsafe buildings
topics.summary: Check before you go back in
steps: Do not enter a building with visible cracks, leaning walls, sagging floors or broken supports.
Wait for an official all-clear before re-entering.
If you must enter, go in daylight, wear sturdy shoes and tell someone where you are.
Leave immediately if you hear creaking or see new cracks.

topics.title: Electrical hazards
topics.summary: Treat wet or damaged wiring as live
steps: Keep away from fallen or sagging power lines and report them to the utility.
Do not switch on power in a flooded or damaged building until it has been checked.
Do not touch electrical equipment while standing in water.
Use a torch, not candles, when checking damaged areas.

topics.title: Fire hazards
topics.summary: Fires often start after a disaster
steps: If you smell gas, open windows, leave and do not use switches or flames.
Keep flammable items away from heaters and stoves.
Do not use damaged gas cylinders or heaters.
Know where your fire extinguisher is.

topics.title: Water safety
topics.summary: Assume water is unsafe until confirmed
steps: Use bottled water or boil water for at least one minute before drinking.
Do not use flood water for drinking, cooking or brushing teeth.
Discard food that touched flood water or has been without refrigeration for hours.

topics.title: Hygiene
topics.summary: Prevent illness while services are disrupted
steps: Wash hands with safe water and soap, especially before eating and after cleaning.
Wear gloves and boots when cleaning up mud or debris.
Keep cuts covered and get medical help for deep wounds or fever.
Dispose of waste away from water sources.

topics.title: Safe return
topics.summary: Go back only when it is safe
steps: Return only when authorities say the area is safe.
Check for gas, water and electricity damage before using them.
Travel in daylight and avoid flooded or damaged roads.
Keep your phone charged and tell a contact when you arrive.

topics.title: Damage documentation
topics.summary: Record damage before you clean up
steps: Take clear photos and short videos of all damage from several angles.
Write down what was damaged, roughly when, and its approximate value.
Keep receipts and damaged items until they have been recorded.
File a damage report in SETU Recovery so it is saved with a time and location.

topics.title: Protecting important documents
topics.summary: Keep identity and property papers safe
steps: Store originals in a waterproof bag or container.
Keep photocopies or photos of ID, property and insurance papers separately.
Dry wet papers flat, away from direct heat, and do not separate stuck pages by force.

topics.title: Contacting authorities
topics.summary: Use official channels for official help
steps: Use your local official emergency channels for urgent help.
Use SETU SOS for a life-threatening emergency, including when the network is down.
Recovery reports in SETU are saved on this device and sent when a route is available. They are not a substitute for calling for urgent help.
Keep the report ID of anything you file.

topics.title: Avoiding unsafe structures
topics.summary: Stay clear of what could fall
steps: Stay away from damaged walls, chimneys, bridges, hoardings and leaning poles.
Do not shelter under damaged roofs or balconies.
Keep children and pets away from debris and damaged buildings.
Do not climb on or move debris that could shift.
